text:
Jordan Kyrou spent eight seasons and nearly 500 games in St. Louis before landing in Washington, and his first months as a Capital have gone better than the box score suggests. He has 5 goals and 14 points in 20 games on 14 and a half minutes a night, half of those points on the power play. Lately the points have dried up: six straight games without one, during a stretch where Washington has lost five in a row.

That drought isn't on him. The chances are there (about 3.8 expected points' worth in those six games), and the Capitals have scored 9.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That has cost him assists and usually swings back. At five on five Washington gets about 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there.

The surprise in his profile is defense. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in and living in the slot. He's playing well. The goals around him just haven't come yet.
